briefing.text: MSI-high colorectal tumours are mostly right-sided and carry BRAF V600E and RNF43 frameshifts (e.g. G659fs), so including them can make BRAF/RNF43 look right-enriched through MSI confounding alone. Tabulate MSI_STATUS (MSS/MSI/Inconclusive/NA) by PRIMARY_TUMOR_LOCATION in data_clinical_sample.txt and analyse MSS only. Many samples (about 327) have MSI_STATUS=NA but an MSI_SCORE; decide explicitly how to handle them (e.g. MSIsensor cut-offs: <3 MSS, 3-10 indeterminate, >=10 MSI-H) and report results both for strict MSI_STATUS==MSS and for score-derived MSS.
briefing.reason: The hypothesis is restricted to MSS; the MSS definition and NA handling directly change the analysed cohort and can create spurious enrichment.

briefing.text: The hypothesis concerns metastatic CRC, but the cohort includes MCRC_TYPE='Early Stage Primary' samples (about 123) and about 14 samples with PRIMARY_TUMOR_LOCATION=NA. Tabulate MCRC_TYPE and PRIMARY_TUMOR_LOCATION; run the main analysis on mCRC samples (mCRC Primary + mCRC Metastasis) with known Left/Right side, and include early-stage samples only as a sensitivity analysis. Standard convention: right = caecum to transverse colon (proximal to splenic flexure), left = splenic flexure to rectum. Check PRIMARY_SITE against the provided Right/Left label; transverse colon handling varies and rectum may behave differently from left colon.
briefing.reason: Defines the correct population (metastatic) and the exposure variable (sidedness); both are easy to get wrong.

briefing.text: About 31 patients have more than one sequenced sample (e.g. primary and metastasis). Count SAMPLE_ID per PATIENT_ID among MSS samples with known side and collapse to one row per patient before testing (either altered-if-any-sample-altered, or one prespecified sample such as the primary). Primary-metastasis concordance is high for KRAS/BRAF but lower for PIK3CA, so state the rule used.
briefing.reason: Duplicate patients double-count and break independence in Fisher tests.

briefing.text: Samples were sequenced on different MSK-IMPACT panels (IMPACT341/410/468). Genes added in later panels (RNF43 may be absent from IMPACT341 - verify in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt / panel gene lists, and check whether any RNF43 mutation occurs in IMPACT341 samples) would be wrongly counted as wild-type in samples whose panel did not cover them. Cross-tabulate panel by side, and compute each gene's frequency with a denominator restricted to samples whose panel covers that gene; also exclude samples with mutations=NA in the panel matrix.
briefing.reason: If panel mix differs by side, uncovered genes counted as wild-type bias the side comparison.

briefing.text: The hypothesis is about ONCOGENIC alterations, and the mutation file has no OncoKB/oncogenic annotation column. List Variant_Classification and protein changes for KRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, AKT1, RNF43, SMAD4, and define 'oncogenic' a priori before testing, e.g. KRAS G12/G13/Q61/K117/A146; BRAF V600 and class 2/3 kinase-domain variants; PIK3CA hotspots (E542/E545/H1047 etc.); AKT1 E17K; truncating mutations in RNF43 and SMAD4, plus SMAD4 deep deletions (value -2) from data_cna.txt. Report results under both an 'any non-synonymous' and a 'hotspot/truncating' definition and check whether the conclusion holds under both. Exclude silent/intronic rows.
briefing.reason: The alteration definition determines the counts; counting VUS/passengers inflates frequencies, and CNA data are needed for SMAD4.

briefing.text: Hypermutated MSS tumours (e.g. POLE exonuclease-domain mutants, aa 268-471; TMB often >50 mut/Mb) carry many incidental mutations in KRAS/BRAF/PIK3CA etc. and can inflate frequencies on whichever side they fall. Inspect TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS among MSS samples, POLE exonuclease mutations, and MSI_SCORE values in the 3-10 range, and run a sensitivity analysis excluding hypermutated MSS samples (e.g. TMB>20).
briefing.reason: A few hypermutators can drive apparent side differences within the MSS group.

briefing.text: The hypothesis names six genes. Do not judge it on a single pooled 'any of six altered' test or on one gene alone. Run per-gene 2x2 Fisher tests (right vs left, MSS, one row per patient, panel-aware denominators), report odds ratios with 95% CI, direction of each effect, and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted q-values. Decide in advance how the per-gene results map to a label: consider how many genes show right-side enrichment, whether the main ones are significant after FDR correction, and whether any gene is significantly enriched in the opposite direction. Rare genes (e.g. AKT1) may be underpowered; an underpowered non-significant result is not by itself a contradiction.
briefing.reason: Gives a prespecified multi-gene decision rule and multiple-testing control, so the label is not driven by one gene or by uncorrected p-values.

shared_assumptions: Both teams take PRIMARY_TUMOR_LOCATION as the side label as given: Transverse colon is split 35 Right / 19 Left, one Cecum sample is labelled Left, Rectum (261) counts as Left, and 'Colon'/NA are dropped. Neither re-derived side from PRIMARY_SITE or tested it with rectum excluded or transverse colon dropped.

Both treat one Fisher test per gene on a pooled set of primary and metastasis samples as the comparison. Neither stratified by SAMPLE_TYPE or MCRC_TYPE, so primary-versus-metastasis mix could differ between the two sides.

Both assume a hand-made hotspot/truncating rule stands in for 'oncogenic'. The MAF has no OncoKB or hotspot column, and neither team checked how sensitive the rule is per gene (for example SMAD4 missense, or RNF43 G659fs, a known recurrent frameshift that is often treated as MSI-associated).
Both read 'True' as all six genes pointing the same way, even though SMAD4 and AKT1 are not individually significant.
unused_evidence: data_sv.txt holds structural variants in the hypothesis genes (BRAF fusions/deletions, RNF43 rearrangements, SMAD4 deletion/translocation). Neither method lists using it. The events are few, but for low-count genes (SMAD4, BRAF fusions) they could move borderline results.
MCRC_TYPE (mCRC Primary / mCRC Metastasis / Early Stage Primary) defines the 'mCRC' population directly. Team B does not say whether the 123 Early Stage Primary samples were excluded.
MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE: 2 MSS-labelled samples have subtype MSI, and 2 NA-MSI samples have subtype MSI. These matter for how MSS is defined.
data_cna_hg19.seg was not used to confirm SMAD4 deep deletions, and the CNA calls also fold in AKT1/KRAS amplification, which neither team discussed.
unresolved_weak_points: SMAD4 is not significant in strict MSS (p=0.17) and AKT1 is very rare. Both teams only reported this. Neither stated in advance a rule for when a six-gene claim counts as supported.
Team A did not check POLE directly beyond a TMB>20 filter, though MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE flags 7 MSS samples as POLE.

Team A's 'altered if any sample altered' collapse gives patients with several samples more chances to be called altered. Team B instead kept one sample per patient, preferring the primary. Neither compared the two approaches.
second_readings: 'Enrichment of oncogenic alterations in KRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, AKT1, RNF43 and SMAD4' can be read gene by gene (each one enriched) or as a set (any alteration in the six genes, or the count per patient). Under the gene-by-gene reading, SMAD4 and AKT1 being non-significant could argue for a different label, or for a qualified one.

'Microsatellite stable mCRC' could mean strict MSI_STATUS=MSS, or MSS plus NA with a low MSI score. It could also mean metastatic patients only (MCRC_TYPE excluding Early Stage Primary), as opposed to all samples.
'Right-sided primary site' could follow PRIMARY_TUMOR_LOCATION or anatomical PRIMARY_SITE. Whether rectum counts as left-sided, or is a separate group, is a convention choice.
challenge.verdict: Moderate trust. Both teams find four genes strongly enriched on the right, with checks against the MSI definition and the panel. But SMAD4 and AKT1 are not individually supported, neither team set a decision rule for a six-gene claim in advance, and sample-type mix, SV events and side-label conventions were left untested.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Rerun the per-gene tests keeping one sample per patient (primary preferred) instead of 'altered if any sample altered', and also stratified by SAMPLE_TYPE (primary vs metastasis), for example with a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test. Do any gene's direction or significance change, and does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Add the SV events in data_sv.txt for BRAF, RNF43 and SMAD4 to your oncogenic definition, and separately exclude the 7 MSS samples with MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE=POLE and the 2 MSS samples with MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE=MSI. Does SMAD4 or AKT1 change, and does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Before you look at results again, write down the rule by which a six-gene enrichment claim is 'supported' (all genes significant, a set-level test, or direction plus a combined test). Then run a set-level test on whether a patient has any oncogenic alteration in the six genes. Does your label follow from that rule, and does it change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Repeat the analysis with rectum excluded, and with Transverse colon and the Cecum|Left sample dropped. Do the per-gene results still point the same way, and does this change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Tabulate MCRC_TYPE in your analysis set and rerun with the 123 Early Stage Primary samples excluded, and separately included. Does any gene's result change, and does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Within your one-sample-per-patient set, check whether the share of metastasis samples differs between Right and Left. Then rerun stratified by SAMPLE_TYPE (for example with a CMH test). Does any gene change direction or significance, and does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Add the BRAF, RNF43 and SMAD4 events from data_sv.txt to your definition. Also tabulate how many RNF43 truncating calls per side are G659fs, and rerun without them. Do the RNF43 and SMAD4 results hold, and does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Write down before looking again the rule by which the six-gene claim counts as supported, then run a set-level test (any oncogenic alteration in the six genes per patient, Right vs Left) next to your per-gene tests. Does your label follow from that rule given SMAD4 p=0.17, and does it change your method?

questions.why: Both teams used a hand-made oncogenic rule. Whether these variant classes count as oncogenic decides the counts for the weakest genes.

questions.question: In colorectal cancer sidedness studies, what are the usual conventions for classifying the transverse colon and the rectum (right, left, or excluded)?
questions.why: The side labels in the data split transverse colon across both groups, and rectum makes up a large part of the left group. A different convention could change the comparison.

findings.question: In colorectal cancer genomics, which oncogenic alteration classes does OncoKB assign to SMAD4 (missense in the MH2 domain, truncating, deep deletion) and to RNF43 (for example the recurrent G659fs frameshift), and is RNF43 G659fs regarded as a passenger linked to microsatellite instability?
findings.answer: SMAD4: Truncating Mutations = Likely Oncogenic (Likely LoF); Deletion (deep deletion) = Likely Oncogenic (LoF); MH2-domain missense are curated variant by variant, with many rated Likely Oncogenic (e.g. R361H/C/G, D351H/N, G352E, G386D, R496H, R497H, W509R, G510R, R515G, D537A/E/G/H/V) and D537Y = Oncogenic. OncoKB lists 55 oncogenic, 4 inconclusive and 1 neutral SMAD4 alterations, and missense variants it has not curated are not automatically oncogenic. RNF43: Truncating Mutations = Likely Oncogenic (Likely LoF), and OncoKB notes they occur mainly in MSI tumours. However, G659fs*41 is curated specifically as Oncogenicity 'Inconclusive' (conflicting data), so under OncoKB it should NOT count as oncogenic even though it is a frameshift. G659Vfs*41 is a 1-bp deletion in a 7-G homopolymer repeat. It occurs almost only in MLH1-low (MSI) tumours, and Tu et al. 2019 showed the mutant protein works like wild type in Wnt inhibition. They concluded it is likely an MSI-driven replication-slippage passenger. A 2022 Nature Communications paper (snippet only, not read in full) dispute this and report a PI3K-activating effect, so the passenger view is widely held but contested. In an MSS cohort G659fs should be rare.

findings.question: In colorectal cancer sidedness studies, what are the usual conventions for classifying the transverse colon and the rectum (right, left, or excluded)?
findings.answer: The most common clinical convention (most mCRC trial series) splits at the splenic flexure. Everything proximal to it, including the entire transverse colon, is right-sided, and the splenic flexure and everything distal to it, including the rectum, is left-sided (left = at least 63% of CRC). The embryological definition splits the transverse colon, with the proximal two-thirds (midgut) on the right and the distal third (hindgut) on the left. The rectum is hindgut and therefore left, but some studies describe the rectum separately (distal colon / proximal colon / rectum) or analyse colon only. Because the transverse colon is ambiguous, many investigators either assign it to the right or exclude it. Loree et al. 2018 (n=1,876) found transverse tumours' mutation clusters looked more left-sided than right-sided. They also found that sigmoid/rectal tumours have fewer PIK3CA, BRAF and CTNNB1 mutations and less MSI than other left-sided sites, so a large rectal share in the left group tends to widen right-versus-left differences for those genes. Splitting the transverse colon or putting the rectum on the left are both standard conventions; a robust analysis could check sensitivity by excluding transverse and/or rectum.
